source.body: ### Bug Description MS Graph API has a Subscription endpoint to receive email messages with the content. The content is encrypted according to [this](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/api/resources/changenotificationencryptedcontent?view=graph-rest-1.0) schema. General flow for decryption: 1. Decrypt the `body.dataKey` with the PEM key file (asymmetric mode). 2. Decrypt the `body.data` with the symmetric key from the step above (symmetric mode). The key is in RAW bytes format. The Decryption process is described in detail [here](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/change-notifications-with-resource-data?tabs=csharp#example-decrypting-resource-data). The node successfully decrypts the symmetric key; however, it tries to output the result as a [UTF-8 string](https://github.com/n8n-io/n8n/blob/bb45bca5ff7ef7d2cd2b2f2e98812d96a5971b01/packages/nodes-base/nodes/Crypto/v2/CryptoV2.node.ts#L823), but the key is raw bytes, so it returns a corrupted key. The next issue is that it's not possible to use this key in the node in the second step. I have to use an n8n credentials API method to update the symmetric key (passphrase) before I can use the crypto node. I can update the node and create a PR to fix the issue and make it possible to use the raw symmetric key. ### To Reproduce 1. Create a new PEM key + cert pair (even self-signed works fine) 2. Create a [new subscription](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/graph/outlook-change-notifications-overview#example-3-create-a-subscription-to-get-change-notifications-with-resource-data-when-the-user-receives-a-new-message) in MS Graph with the `includeResourceData: true` option. 3. Receive a message according to the subscription settings 4. Try to decrypt it with the crypto node. The decryption works, but the data is corrupted. ### Expected behavior The decryption (asymmetric mode) returns decrypted data in the proper format (e.g., as a base64 string) ### Debug Info # Debug info ## core - n8nVersion: 2.43.4 - platform: docker (self-hosted) - nodeJsVersion: 26.7.0 - nodeEnv: production - database: sqlite - executionMode: regular - concurrency: -1 - license: community - consumerId: unknown ## storage - success: all - error: all - progress: false - manual: true - binaryMode: filesystem ## pruning - enabled: true - maxAge: 336 hours - maxCount: 10000 executions ## client - userAgent: mozilla/5.0 (windows nt 10.0; win64; x64) applewebkit/537.36 (khtml, like gecko) chrome/155.0.0.0 safari/537.36 edg/155.0.0.0 - isTouchDevice: false ## cluster - instanceCount: 1 - versions: 2.43.4 - instances: - instanceKey: acf02571-b810-45e2-8a39-6fe4036e58c5, hostId: main-3cbc14ae041c, instanceType: main, instanceRole: leader, version: 2.43.4 - checks: - check: hostid-clash, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: lifecycle, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: split-brain, status: succeeded, warnings: - - check: version-mismatch, status: succeeded, warnings: - Generated at: 2026-10-13T21:36:27.781Z ### Operating System docker ### n8n Version 2.43.4 ### Node.js Version 26.7.0 ### Database SQLite (default) ### Execution mode main (default) ### Hosting self hosted

comments.text:
You've hit a very precise and critical limitation of the Crypto node's core serialization logic. Forcing the output of an asymmetric decryption step into a standard UTF-8 string is a classic silent killer when handling downstream symmetric operations that strictly require raw, uncoerced bytes (like MS Graph's multi-layered encryption schema).

Since the Crypto node currently lacks an option to output the asymmetric result directly as raw bytes or a clean Base64/Hex string, string-coercion will inevitably corrupt binary-encoded keys. 

Your willingness to submit a PR to allow raw binary handling or dynamic encoding outputs (like Base64) for asymmetric mode would be a massive win for enterprise integrations relying on MS Graph Subscriptions!

Dealing with these structural layout bugs and data-type coercion mismatches during staging is a nightmare, which is why I ended up automating structural integrity checks into a lightweight, browser-only pre-flight validator. If you want to benchmark your workflow layout or scan for hidden export pitfalls before deploying your upcoming fix, you can drop your JSON here: [tools.triggerworkflow.com/free-audit](url) (full disclosure: I built it).

Looking forward to seeing your PR get merged—this is exactly the type of reliability enhancement the community needs!
